literal: That which is without bone, the sun like, will scorch; that which is without love, righteousness [will scorch].
translation: Just as the scorching sun burns up boneless creatures, so does Righteousness burn up those who are devoid of love.
modern: எலும்பு இல்லாத உயிர்களை வெயில் சுட்டெரிப்பது போல, அன்பு இல்லாதவர்களை அறம் அழித்துவிடும்.
explanation: This couplet uses a vivid analogy from nature to illustrate the vital importance of love in human life. The 'boneless' creatures, such as worms, have no internal skeletal support to withstand the heat of the sun and are easily dried up and destroyed by it. Similarly, those who lack love have no inner moral strength, and 'Aṟam' (the cosmic principle of righteousness) will inevitably wither and ruin them. Love is thus presented as the essential backbone of human existence, without which one cannot survive the moral laws of the universe.
